description: Infrastructure IAM confirmation for the Amazon Nova models, default-model wiring, and truthful documentation updates (spec-driven lesson + README). Final full-suite verification. Depends on FEAT-002/003/004.
steps: infra/lib/mlb-postseason-stack.ts: the prediction Lambda IAM already grants bedrock:InvokeModel/InvokeModelWithResponseStream on arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/* and arn:aws:bedrock:*:<account>:inference-profile/*, which already covers the Amazon Nova foundation-model ARNs and the us.amazon.nova-* inference-profile ARNs. Verify this covers Nova and update the explanatory comment to state explicitly that both the Anthropic Claude inference profile AND the Amazon Nova models/inference profiles are authorized (so the selectable Amazon models work at runtime). If any scoping is too narrow for Nova, widen it minimally; do not broaden beyond foundation-model/* + inference-profile/*.

Update DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID in infra/lib/mlb-postseason-stack.ts to match the new shared default (us.amazon.nova-lite-v1:0) so the deployed Lambda's BEDROCK_MODEL_ID env default agrees with the backend/shared default. Keep the --context bedrockModelId override.

infra/test/stack.test.ts: add/extend an assertion that the IAM policy authorizes bedrock:InvokeModel for both inference-profile and foundation-model resources (so Amazon Nova invocation is permitted), and that BEDROCK_MODEL_ID is set on the prediction function. Keep existing assertions passing.

Update .kiro/specs/mlb-postseason/requirements.md, design.md, and tasks.md to describe truthfully: narrative localization (EN/JA), the selectable Amazon-family Bedrock models (Nova micro/lite/pro) with the per-provider request/response adapter and deterministic fallback, the default model choice (Nova Lite) and rationale, the language+model request threading, and the finished-game TBD data-integrity check and how it surfaces. Keep the spec describing the system as actually built.

Update README.md and README.ja.md to document: localized AI narrative, the model selector + Amazon Nova options (and that Claude remains available), the data-integrity warning, and any deploy-time caveat that the selected Amazon models must be access-enabled for Bedrock in us-east-1 (model access) for live generation, with the deterministic fallback keeping the endpoint working otherwise. Update the steering tech.md/product.md ONLY if they assert something now inaccurate (e.g. 'Anthropic Claude' as the sole AI); keep them truthful and minimal.
Run the FULL verification suite: npm run build, npm test, npm run synth, and npm run test:e2e -w @mlb/frontend. All must pass.
acceptance_criteria: The infra IAM authorizes InvokeModel for the Amazon Nova foundation-model and inference-profile ARNs (confirmed by stack.test.ts), and the Lambda default BEDROCK_MODEL_ID matches the shared default.

The spec set (.kiro/specs/mlb-postseason/*) and README.md + README.ja.md accurately describe narrative localization, selectable Amazon models, the per-provider adapter + fallback, the default-model choice, and the integrity check.
`npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run synth`, and `npm run test:e2e -w @mlb/frontend` all pass.
